quickAnswerHtml: Praprai is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Khon Kaen, in the Ban Phet area (near Khon Kaen airport). Budget around 101–250, and it's mostly walk-in/queue at the door

blocks.html:
Ask anyone in Khon Kaen which restaurant is their go-to before a flight, and the answer you'll hear so often it's practically a local joke is "Praprai the airport one" — a nickname locals have used for decades, because this old-school Isan restaurant has sat right by the entrance to Khon Kaen airport for that long. It's barely 300 meters from the airport gate. Anyone with an evening flight swings by for one last full meal before heading home, and it's become a tradition for both Khon Kaen locals and the out-of-towners who work in the area. The restaurant's reputation isn't just about location, though — it's the straightforward, honest Isan cooking that earned it a Bib Gourmand from the MICHELIN Guide Thailand, and it's kept its place on Khon Kaen's list of 11 MICHELIN restaurants for the 2026 edition too. A Bib Gourmand is the seal that says "genuinely good food at a price that doesn't sting" — a description that fits this place perfectly, since a real meal here runs you just over a hundred baht a head.

The dish both MICHELIN and reviewers single out as the restaurant's signature is the fried fermented fish — fish fermented until it hits that perfect sour-salty balance, then fried until the skin turns crisp and the flesh stays firm, topped with crispy fried herbs. Eaten with hot sticky rice, it's the dish that defines this place. If you've had fried fermented fish elsewhere and shrugged, try it here before you judge. Beyond that, the menu runs fully Isan and som tum territory, and what you should order next is the crispy pork peanut som tum — full-on Isan-spicy pounded salad cut with crispy, fatty pork — plus banana-leaf-wrapped mushroom mok, which gets harder to find in big cities every year, a light and herbal fish omok, and tangy, funky Isan sausage that makes a great snack while you wait for the rest of the table.

What makes Praprai worth loving is exactly how Khon Kaen it is. Khon Kaen is the unofficial capital of Isan food, full of serious eaters with opinions about flavor. A restaurant that's survived this long among the hundreds of som tum shops across the city has been tested by local palates over and over again — and getting a MICHELIN stamp on top of that just confirms it: this isn't a place that's popular because of a trend, it's popular because it's been cooking good food for so long the whole city vouches for it. If you've just landed in Khon Kaen and don't know where to start your first meal, walk straight here from the terminal. Or save it as your last meal in town before you fly out — either way works just as well.

blocks.name: Praprai
blocks.descHtml:
Praprai sits in the Ban Phet area, right by the entrance to Khon Kaen airport, about 300 meters from the airport gate — an easy walk. Budget runs 101–250 THB per person (MICHELIN rates it ฿฿). It's walk-in only, no advance booking, with hours roughly 11:00–21:00, closed Mondays — though Wongnai shows it open only on certain days from 11:00–20:00, so it's worth calling ahead to confirm at 081-974-9853 or 043-055287, especially if you're planning to stop by before a flight.

An important tip if you're on a flight schedule: some Wongnai reviews mention food coming out slowly when the restaurant is busy, so build in extra time before your flight to avoid the stress. Lunch and evenings on Friday-Sunday get especially busy since it's a popular stop for travelers passing through — if you'd rather eat at a relaxed pace, go in the early afternoon lull instead. If getting to the restaurant isn't convenient, delivery is available through Wongnai x LINE MAN. Dress is casual. Follow the restaurant on Facebook: prapraikhonkaen

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at Praprai in Khon Kaen?
faq.a: No booking needed — it's walk-in only. Hours are inconsistent between sources (TrueID says roughly 11:00–21:00, closed Mondays, while Wongnai shows it open only certain days 11:00–20:00), so it's best to call ahead to confirm at 081-974-9853 or 043-055287

faq.q: About how much per person at Praprai?
faq.a: Around 101–250 THB per person according to Wongnai, while MICHELIN rates the price level ฿฿ — a Bib Gourmand meal for just over a hundred baht a head

faq.q: What should I order at Praprai?
faq.a: The signature dish, according to both MICHELIN and reviewers, is the fried fermented fish with a perfect sour-salty balance, topped with crispy fried herbs, followed by crispy pork peanut som tum, banana-leaf mushroom mok, fish omok, and Isan sausage

faq.q: Where is Praprai and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's in the Ban Phet area, right by the entrance to Khon Kaen airport, about 300 meters from the airport gate — ideal for a meal before your flight or right after landing. During busy periods food can come out slowly, so build in extra time if you're on a flight schedule. If getting there isn't convenient, delivery is available through Wongnai x LINE MAN
